gold.title: Off-by-one error in the loop condition: `i <= startIndex + pageSize` iterates pageSize + 1 times instead of pageSize tim
gold.description: Off-by-one error in the loop condition: `i <= startIndex + pageSize` iterates pageSize + 1 times instead of pageSize times. The condition should be `i < startIndex + pageSize`. This causes each page to return one extra element (stealing the first item from the next page), breaking pagination boundaries and producing inconsistent results across pages.

candidate.title: Pagination loop is off by one — returns pageSize + 1 items and overlaps adjacent pages
candidate.description: Loop iterates pageSize + 1 times using `i <= startIndex + pageSize`. Causes duplicate items at page boundaries (e.g., paginate(['a','b','c','d','e'], 1, 2) returns 3 items instead of 2, with 'c' appearing in both page 1 and page 2). Page boundary items duplicated across pages; items.length never matches advertised pageSize. Fix: use const items = data.slice(startIndex, startIndex + pageSize).
